notes.C01: One signal across speech and frames does demotion, caption skip and tagging, with a clear bench test.
notes.C02: Deletes the metered VLM, the biggest running cost, but rests on retrieval quality that is unproven.
notes.C03: Return map is useful on recurring footage but adds layout logic gated by a measured ratio.
notes.C04: Replaces proven keyframe heuristics with embedding of every sample, so it risks cost and regressions.
notes.C05: Ask-conditioned sheets with a coverage floor are sound but close to the already-proposed find command.
notes.C06: Text-only default cuts tokens sharply but drifts from the user's stated goal of sending image grids.
notes.C07: Checking the agent's own summary against frames is a fresh, label-free grounding loop and doubles as a bench score.
notes.C08: Three-modality agreement is tidy but needs the audio tower and has weak payoff.
notes.C09: Per-video calibration removes knobs but adds its own calibration machinery and fallback states.
notes.C10: Admission gate is disciplined, but the value is only a tag line for silent windows.
notes.C11: A paired-arm bench is the cheap way to prove every other idea, though it is meta and not new.
notes.C12: An audit sheet and a gap trace make omissions visible, but they are diagnostics and not new capability.
notes.C13: Recording deletions in decisions is good hygiene, but it is process and does not use the model.
notes.C14: Cheap, concrete recall test for the MRL dimension that also shrinks signals.npz, but small in impact.
notes.C15: A scope-tracking checklist is process about the session and not a use of the model, so it answers a different question.
